steps.prompt: Which of these could you write a whole essay to prove?
steps.a: Chocolate ice cream is the best flavour.
steps.b: Schools should serve fewer sugary desserts at lunch.
steps.reveal: A is a personal taste: nobody can prove what tastes best. B is a claim: people could disagree, and you could prove it with reasons and evidence about health, focus and cost.

cards.title: Three kinds of statement
cards.body: A fact is true or false and can be checked: “Our school has 600 students.” An opinion is a personal taste: “Blue is the nicest colour.” A claim is a position someone could disagree with, that you can support with reasons and evidence: “Our school should add a second lunch period.”

cards.title: Words that make a claim
cards.body: Claims often use should, must, need to, better, worse, more important, ban or allow. A fact has nothing to argue about. An opinion has nothing to prove. A thesis is always a claim (or, in an informative essay, a focus).

cards.title: From opinion to claim
cards.showing: Recess should be at least thirty minutes long because children need to move to focus.
cards.note: The claim says what should change, and why. Now there is something to prove.

prompts: How can you tell a claim from an opinion?
Which of your claims would make the best essay? Why?
